newsitem.title: Turkmenistan: Turkmenistan sees 1997 oil, gas output rising.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan sees 1997 oil, gas output rising.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Turkmenistan plans to increase its natural gas output in 1997 to 53 billion cubic metres (bcm), up from 35 bcm last year, the official press said on Tuesday.
The new gas target is above an earlier figure of 44 bcm announced by Niyazov last year.
Under Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov's new economic plan, the country also plans to produce six million tonnes of oil and gas condensate in 1997, up from last year's 4.3 million tonnes.
Under a 1996 agreement with Russia's gas monopoly Gazprom, Turkmenistan is set to export about 20 bcm to western Europe this year.

Former Oil and Gas Minister Gochmurad Nazdzhanov said last month that the country aimed in the long term to produce about 85 bcm a year and said it had estimated reserves of 21 trillion cubic metres of gas and 6.5 billion tonnes of oil.
